title: Report of the Committee on Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of Artificial Intelligence (FREE-AI) in the Financial Sector
issuing_body: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

timeline.event: RBI Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies announces a committee to develop a FREE-AI framework
Committee constituted by RBI
Report released on RBI website with 7 sutras and 26 recommendations
RBI issues draft Guidance on Regulatory Principles for Model Risk Management, the first follow-on regulatory text covering AI/ML models

summary: Committee report setting out a voluntary framework for AI adoption by RBI-regulated entities, organised around seven principles ('sutras') and six pillars, with 26 recommendations addressed to RBI, regulated entities and government.
key_provisions: Seven sutras: Trust is the Foundation; People First; Innovation over Restraint; Fairness and Equity; Accountability; Understandable by Design; Safety, Resilience and Sustainability
26 recommendations grouped under six pillars: Infrastructure, Policy, Capacity (innovation enablement) and Governance, Protection, Assurance (risk mitigation)
Recommends shared financial-sector data and compute infrastructure, an AI innovation sandbox and indigenous financial-sector AI models
Recommends board-approved AI policies at regulated entities, an AI incident reporting mechanism, consumer protection and liability measures, and an AI audit framework
Report is recommendatory; it creates no obligations on regulated entities by itself
confidence_note: RBI press release read; report PDF located on rbidocs but its full text (including committee chair and the individual recommendation wording) was not read in this session. Sutras and pillars confirmed by two secondary summaries.

title: Draft Guidance on Regulatory Principles for Model Risk Management, 2026
issuing_body: Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Department of Regulation

timeline.event: Draft guidance released for public comment
Comment window closes (via 'Connect 2 Regulate' or email to Operational Risk Group, Department of Regulation)

summary: Draft RBI guidance proposing lifecycle governance requirements for all models used by regulated entities, expressly including third-party models and models using AI/ML. Final version not traced as of 19 November 2026.
key_provisions: Applies to 11 classes of regulated entities: commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks, regional rural banks, urban and rural co-operative banks, all-India financial institutions, NBFCs, asset reconstruction companies and credit information companies
Scope covers 'all models used by regulated entities, including third party models and models employing AI / ML'
Requires a board-approved Model Risk Management Framework, a model inventory (no model to be used unless inventoried) and risk-based tiering of models
Higher-tier models require independent validation, closer monitoring and approval by the board's Risk Management Committee (per secondary summaries)
Regulated entities remain accountable for third-party model outcomes; due diligence, documentation access, audit rights and exit arrangements expected
Comments invited until 24 July 2026
confidence_note: RBI press release read (date, scope, deadline). Detailed requirements (tiering, third-party clauses) taken from law-firm and industry summaries of the draft. No final guidance located as of 19 Nov 2026; status remains consultation (closed).

title: MuleHunter.AI (Reserve Bank Innovation Hub)
issuing_body: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) / Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH)

timeline.event: RBI Governor's statement announces MuleHunter.AI pilot with two public sector banks and encourages banks to collaborate with RBIH
Reported as deployed across 31 banks (date approximate; reported by industry sources)

summary: An AI/ML model developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub to detect mule accounts used to launder fraud proceeds; RBI encouraged (but did not mandate) banks to adopt it.
key_provisions: Built on analysis of 19 patterns of mule-account behaviour identified with partner banks
Piloted with two large public sector banks in late 2024; later reported live at 31 banks
Offered to banks as a supervisory-encouraged tool, not a regulatory mandate
Positioned alongside RBI's Digital Payments Intelligence Platform workstream on fraud
confidence_note: RBIH documentation page and press coverage of the 6 Dec 2024 Governor's statement agree. '31 banks' figure from a single industry source and not verified against RBI.

title: Reporting for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) applications and systems offered and used by market intermediaries / MIIs / mutual funds
issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

timeline.event: Circular SEBI/HO/MIRSD/DOS2/CIR/P/2019/10 for market intermediaries
Parallel circular for market infrastructure institutions (reported)
Circular extending quarterly AI/ML reporting to mutual funds

summary: SEBI circulars requiring intermediaries, exchanges/depositories and mutual funds to file a quarterly AI/ML reporting form describing AI/ML systems offered to investors or used internally.
key_provisions: Quarterly AI/ML Reporting Form to be submitted within 15 days of quarter end (via exchanges/depositories for intermediaries)
Covers applications offered to investors or used internally for investing, trading, advice dissemination and all fintech/regtech initiatives using AI/ML
Stated objectives: inventory AI/ML use, confirm compliance with SEBI cyber security framework, and record safeguards against data breach and system failure
Still the only SEBI AI-specific obligation in force as of November 2026; a wider framework is pending (see 2025 consultation)
confidence_note: Circular text read via NSDL-hosted copy (not sebi.gov.in). MII circular date of 31 Jan 2019 is from memory of secondary coverage and should be checked.

title: Safer participation of retail investors in Algorithmic trading (SEBI circular)
issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

timeline.event: Consultation paper on retail algo trading released (reported)
Circular SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD/P/CIR/2025/0000013 issued; original effective date 1 Aug 2025
Circular extends implementation to 1 Oct 2025
Framework takes effect

summary: SEBI framework under which retail investors may use algorithmic trading only through registered brokers, with each algo approved by the exchange, APIs tagged, and algo providers empanelled; relevant to AI-driven trading strategies.
key_provisions: Retail investors may access algos only via registered stock brokers; brokers need exchange permission for each algo
Algo providers act as agents of brokers (principal-agent relationship); exchanges to empanel algo providers
All algo orders tagged with a unique identifier; API access via static IP and secure authentication
Retail investors developing their own algos above an order-per-second threshold must register the algo through the broker (threshold set by exchanges)
Effective 1 October 2025 after extension from 1 August 2025
confidence_note: Circular number, date and extension confirmed from an exchange-hosted copy and legal summaries; sebi.gov.in URL not captured. Order-per-second threshold detail from secondary sources.

title: Consultation Paper on Guidelines for Responsible Usage of AI/ML in Indian Securities Markets
issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

timeline.event: Consultation paper released
Comment window closes
SEBI Chairman says detailed AI/ML guidelines will be issued, built on disclosure, accountability and human-in-the-loop; no final circular yet

summary: SEBI proposal for principle-based guidelines on AI/ML use by market participants, with five pillars and tiered obligations depending on whether the AI affects clients. Final guidelines were still pending as of 16 November 2026.
key_provisions: Five guiding principles: model governance; investor protection and disclosure; testing framework; fairness and bias; data privacy and cyber security
Participants to maintain internal technical teams to monitor models, document development and handle exceptions; senior management oversight and independent audit
Disclosure to clients where AI/ML directly affects them (algo trading, advisory, portfolio management), covering purpose, risks, accuracy and limitations
Pre-deployment testing in simulated environments and continuous monitoring; input/output logs and documentation retained for at least five years
Models must not discriminate between client segments; technical glitches and data breaches to be reported to SEBI
Responsibility for third-party AI remains with the regulated participant
confidence_note: Consultation content confirmed by several secondary sources and a hosted copy of the paper; sebi.gov.in URL not captured in this session. Status (final still pending) confirmed by MediaNama report of the Chairman's 16 Nov 2026 remarks.

title: Advisory on emerging advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools for vulnerability detection (and constitution of the cyber-suraksha.ai task force)
issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), Information Technology Department

timeline.event: Advisory HO/13/19/12(1)2026-ITD-1_CIMGI/10873/2026 issued; task force constituted

summary: SEBI advisory alerting regulated entities to AI tools capable of rapid vulnerability discovery, requiring software bills of materials for critical applications and constituting a cross-industry 'cyber-suraksha.ai' task force.
key_provisions: Regulated entities to maintain current Software Bills of Materials for all critical applications, including open-source components

Constitutes a 'cyber-suraksha.ai' task force of MIIs, qualified RTAs and qualified regulated entities to devise uniform mitigation strategies, share threat intelligence, prioritise incident reporting and review third-party vendor security posture
Reinforces obligations under SEBI's Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF)
Contact point: project-cyber-suraksha.ai@sebi.gov.in
confidence_note: Official SEBI page located (circular number and date read); substantive content taken from a single security-industry summary. Binding effect is mixed: SBOM maintenance reads as an expectation under CSCRF, task-force participation is organisational.

title: Working Group on Artificial Intelligence (WG-AI) for the insurance sector
issuing_body: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

timeline.event: Office Order IRDAI/GA&HR/ORD/MISC/90/06/2026 constitutes seven-member working group
Three-month deadline for recommendations to Member (F&I); report not public as of 19 Nov 2026

summary: IRDAI office order constituting a working group to recommend an AI governance framework for insurers and intermediaries; no IRDAI AI-specific rule exists yet.
key_provisions: Chair: Prof. Sandeep K. Shukla (Director, IIIT Hyderabad); members from ReBIT (former CEO), CERT-In, SBI Life, Star Health, ICICI Lombard; IRDAI CISO as convener

Terms of reference: assess AI adoption and governance maturity, review global approaches, propose a framework for ethical, transparent and explainable AI (including claims and fraud prevention), AI-driven cyber risk, stress-testing, audit standards and capacity building
Recommendations due within three months of constitution
No binding obligations created; outcome expected to feed a future IRDAI framework
confidence_note: Order number, date, composition and ToR reproduced by TaxGuru and trade press; the IRDAI order PDF itself was not retrieved. Whether the group has reported is unverified.

title: IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines, 2026
issuing_body: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

timeline.event: Previous Information and Cyber Security Guidelines 2023 (superseded)
Circular IRDAI/GA&HR/CIR/MISC/51/4/2026 issues revised guidelines, compliance from FY 2026-27

summary: Revised binding cyber security guidelines for insurers, intermediaries, foreign reinsurance branches and the Insurance Information Bureau; relevant as the compliance baseline onto which the IRDAI AI working group's framework is expected to be added.
key_provisions: Applies to all insurers, every class of intermediary (brokers, corporate agents, TPAs, web aggregators, repositories, marketing firms), foreign reinsurance branches and IIB
Compliance required from the current financial year (FY 2026-27) with no stated transition period
Expanded controls on cloud security, third-party and supply-chain risk, incident response and data protection; industry summaries cite 24 domain policies and 347 audit controls
AI-specific content is limited: one compliance vendor states the guidelines contain no AI governance domain; other sources claim an AI cyber-readiness reporting ask by 22 May 2026 (unverified)
confidence_note: Circular number and date agree across sources; the 175-page PDF is hosted by MediaNama/caalley rather than retrieved from irdai.gov.in. Sources conflict on whether there is an AI-specific reporting requirement.

title: Advisory on Heightened Cyber Security Risks arising from Frontier Artificial Intelligence (AI) Models
issuing_body: International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), Division of Cyber Security

timeline.event: Circular IFSCA-CSD/MSC/3/2026-DCS issued to all regulated entities and MIIs in IFSCs, effective immediately

summary: IFSCA circular directing GIFT City regulated entities to treat frontier-AI-enabled cyber attacks as a specific risk scenario, with board review, vendor assurance and governance of internal AI tool use.
key_provisions: Regulated entities to include frontier-AI cyber risk as a specific scenario in cyber risk assessments, with periodic Board review
Treat newly disclosed critical vulnerabilities as exploitable within hours; prepare for rapid 'patch waves'
Critical service providers must assess frontier-AI risks and evidence preparedness for faster exploit timelines
Entities using AI-assisted vulnerability detection must obtain authorisation, avoid sharing sensitive data externally and ensure human oversight before deployment
To be read with IFSCA's existing cyber security and cyber resilience guidelines; proportionality principle applies
confidence_note: Three independent secondary summaries agree on date, reference number and content; the ifsca.gov.in circular PDF was not located. Binding nature is mixed: issued as a circular with 'expectations' rather than numbered obligations.

title: Pension Sahayak AI-enabled grievance portal (PFRDA)
issuing_body: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)

timeline.event: Pension Sahayak launched, replacing the Central Grievance Management System

summary: PFRDA's AI-driven grievance redressal platform for NPS/APY subscribers; recorded here because no PFRDA circular or guideline governing AI use by pension intermediaries was found.
key_provisions: Omnichannel (web, mobile, WhatsApp) AI-assisted grievance handling replacing CGMS
No PFRDA AI governance circular, consultation or committee located as of 19 Nov 2026
confidence_note: Single secondary source for the launch; PFRDA press release not located. Included mainly to record the absence of a PFRDA AI rule.

title: Ethical Guidelines for Application of Artificial Intelligence in Biomedical Research and Healthcare
issuing_body: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Department of Health Research

timeline.event: Guidelines released (ISBN 978-93-5811-343-3); described as a living document

summary: ICMR's first ethical framework for AI in health research and care, addressed to developers, researchers, clinicians, ethics committees, sponsors and funders.
key_provisions: Ten patient-centric principles including autonomy, safety and risk minimisation, trustworthiness, data privacy, accountability and liability, optimisation of data quality, accessibility and equity, collaboration, non-discrimination and fairness, validity
Requires ethics committee review of AI health research and clinical/field validation of AI tools before deployment
Addresses informed consent, data governance and sharing, and human oversight in diagnostic and prognostic AI
Non-binding guidance; enforcement operates through institutional ethics committees and ICMR funding conditions
confidence_note: ICMR page read and official PDF located; exact day of release not shown on the ICMR page (press coverage dated 27 March 2023). Principle list from MediaNama summary.

title: Draft Guidance Document on Medical Device Software (CDSCO)
issuing_body: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), Medical Devices Division

timeline.event: Draft guidance on medical device software released for stakeholder comment
Superseded by final Guidance Document CDSCO/MD/GD/MDSW/01/2026

summary: Draft CDSCO guidance clarifying how software, including AI/ML-based software, is regulated as a medical device under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017.
key_provisions: Proposed that software with a medical purpose (standalone or embedded) is a medical device under MDR 2017 and classified in Classes A to D
Set out expectations on software lifecycle, cybersecurity, interoperability and post-market obligations
Introduced AI/ML-specific considerations later carried into the final guidance
confidence_note: Draft date confirmed by two secondary sources; the draft PDF on cdsco.gov.in was not retrieved.

title: Guidance Document on Medical Device Software (CDSCO/MD/GD/MDSW/01/2026)
issuing_body: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), Medical Devices & IVD Division

timeline.event: Draft guidance released
Final guidance issued under circular F. No. MED-16028/2/2025-eoffice

summary: CDSCO guidance on how software, expressly including AI/ML-enabled software with a medical purpose, is regulated under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, including an Algorithm Change Protocol for AI model updates.
key_provisions: AI/ML software with a medical purpose is a medical device; classified in Classes A-D under MDR 2017 based on significance of information and severity of the healthcare situation (no separate AI class)
Algorithm Change Protocol with five components: data management plan, performance evaluation and monitoring plan, retraining plan, software update plan and rollback plan
Major changes still require approval and minor changes notification to the licensing authority; the protocol does not remove filing

Technical documentation must disclose composition and source of training, validation and test datasets; models trained on non-Indian data need justification of applicability to Indian clinical settings
Bias to be documented in the risk management file; post-market monitoring for performance drift; Software Bill of Materials expected
Guidance states it is for awareness and not for legal purposes; obligations flow from the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and MDR 2017
confidence_note: Official PDF retrieved (document number and disclaimer read). Circular date of 21 July 2026 per National Law Review; one trade outlet gives 23 July 2026.

title: Guidelines on Ethical Advertising and Public Communication by Hospitals/Medical Institutions and Registered Medical Practitioners
issuing_body: National Medical Commission (NMC), Ethics and Medical Registration Board

timeline.event: Public Notice No. R-13014/01/2024-Ethics issues guidelines with immediate effect

summary: NMC guidelines regulating medical advertising, with specific prohibitions on AI-generated testimonials, synthetic patient imagery and misleading AI-assisted claims, enforceable through disciplinary action against registered practitioners.
key_provisions: AI must not be used to create or manipulate a patient's image, voice, testimonial or clinical outcome, or a synthetic endorsement
Section 7.2: AI-generated or AI-assisted content must not create misleading impressions, deceptive outcomes or exaggerated treatment claims
Where AI alteration could affect audience understanding, disclosure is required; permitted AI-generated promotional material must be marked as AI-generated
Graduated penalties (Section 10): warning and ethics training; censure and monetary penalty; 3-6 month suspension; 6-12 months for cure claims or inducements; 1-3 year removal for repeat violations
Issued following proceedings in W.P.(C) 1160/2023 before the Supreme Court; effective immediately
confidence_note: Date, notice number and AI clauses agree across several secondary sources quoting the notice; the nmc.org.in PDF was not retrieved.

title: Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India (SAHI) and BODH benchmarking platform
issuing_body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare / National Health Authority (NHA)

timeline.event: SAHI and BODH launched by the Union Health Minister at the India AI Impact Summit, New Delhi
PIB backgrounder describes SAHI as a recommendatory national framework
NHA reported to be finalising an implementation roadmap with lead agencies, timelines and resources
Government announces AI-led upgrade of Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (claims automation, fraud detection, AI voice scribe linked to ABHA)

summary: National recommendatory strategy for AI in the health system with 32 recommendations across five pillars, accompanied by BODH, an NHA/IIT Kanpur platform for benchmarking health AI models on anonymised Indian data under ABDM.
key_provisions: 32 recommendations across five pillars: governance, regulation and trust; health data and digital infrastructure; workforce and institutional capacity; research, innovation and evidence; ecosystem enablement and global leadership
BODH (Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI) recognised as a digital public good under ABDM; allows model testing against anonymised Indian health data without data leaving source
Framework is expressly recommendatory; accountability mechanisms to come via the NHA implementation roadmap under preparation (Nov 2026)
Builds on the National Health Stack and ABDM; AI voice scribe outputs require doctor approval before linking to ABHA records
confidence_note: PIB backgrounder (official) read in part and confirms recommendatory status, five pillars and BODH; the SAHI document on abdm.gov.in was not itself read. Exact launch day within the February 2026 summit not confirmed.

title: Recommendations on Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Big Data in Telecommunication Sector
issuing_body: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)

timeline.event: Consultation paper released (August 2022)
Recommendations sent to DoT (Press Release No. 62/2023)

summary: TRAI's statutory recommendations to DoT under NDCP 2018 para 2.2(g), proposing a cross-sector AI regulator (AIDAI), a risk-based framework and telecom-specific AI uses. No formal DoT acceptance was traced.
key_provisions: Proposes an independent statutory Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority of India (AIDAI) with a multi-stakeholder advisory body
Recommends a risk-based regulatory framework with legally binding obligations for high-risk AI use cases affecting people
Telecom use cases: AI/ML for duplicate-SIM detection (ASTRA), spam call/message filtering, grievance dashboards for the DoT Public Grievance Unit
Recommendations are advisory to DoT under section 11 of the TRAI Act; DoT response not located
confidence_note: TRAI press release URL located; content confirmed by MediaNama summary. DoT's formal response (acceptance/back-reference) could not be found.

title: Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference (Amendment) Regulations, 2025
issuing_body: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)

timeline.event: TRAI direction requires access providers to deploy AI/ML-based unsolicited commercial communication detection systems (reported)
TCCCPR 2018 amended (February 2025) to mandate proactive monitoring and tighter thresholds

summary: Amendment to the 2018 spam regulations requiring access providers to proactively detect and act on spam, including through AI/ML systems and honeypots, with shorter complaint and action windows.
key_provisions: Complaint window extended from 3 to 7 days; action threshold reduced to 5 complaints in 10 days (from 10 in 7); action within 5 days (from 30)
Mandates proactive, AI/ML-based detection of unregistered senders, spoofed headers and abnormal sending patterns, supported by honeypot numbers (per legal summaries)
Commercial communications restricted to 140 (promotional) and 1600 (transactional/service) series; registered headers mandatory
Access providers empowered to suspend telecom resources of violators; graded financial disincentives on providers
confidence_note: Exact gazette date and the June 2023 direction date were not confirmed against trai.gov.in in this session; the AI/ML detection mandate is reported by industry sources rather than quoted from the regulation text.

title: TRAI Direction on sharing of AI-flagged suspected spammer details among access providers
issuing_body: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)

timeline.event: Direction issued under TCCCPR framework
30-day compliance deadline

summary: Binding TRAI direction requiring telecom operators to share identifiers of numbers flagged by their AI/ML spam-detection systems with all other operators within two hours over the DLT platform, with KYC identifiers within one business day.
key_provisions: Flagging based on behavioural parameters (call volume, duration, velocity, recipient diversity)
Suspected-spam identifiers to be shared with other networks within two hours via the blockchain-based DLT platform
Sender's unique KYC identifiers to be shared within one business day; other operators to identify further numbers held by the same person
Enforcement triggers when five or more numbers of the same person are flagged within ten days across networks
Compliance within 30 days of issue
confidence_note: Single detailed news source (MediaNama) describing a TRAI direction; trai.gov.in direction PDF not located in this session.

title: Consultation on Draft Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026
issuing_body: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), Quality of Service Division

timeline.event: Draft third amendment released for consultation (listed as closed on TRAI site)

summary: TRAI consultation proposing further TCCCPR amendments, including a lower threshold for action on spam flagged by operators' AI systems and provisions on AI-based telemarketing, AI disclosures and consent verification. Final regulation not traced.
key_provisions: Proposes lowering the threshold for action against senders flagged by telcos' AI detection systems
Considers rules for AI-driven telemarketing calls, disclosure that a caller is AI, and consent verification systems
Consultation listed as closed on TRAI's consultation page; final regulations not located as of 19 Nov 2026
confidence_note: Title and date confirmed on TRAI's consultation listing; proposal content from Business Standard headline and a legal commentary. Draft text not read.

title: Draft Guidelines on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services
issuing_body: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), Network, Spectrum and Licensing Division

timeline.event: Draft guidelines released as a consultation paper
Comment deadline

summary: TRAI consultation proposing governance obligations for telecom licensees deploying AI in networks and services: board-approved AI policy, a governance committee, risk classes, an AI inventory, incident reporting and consumer grievance handling. Open for comment as of 19 November 2026.
key_provisions: Board-approved AI policy reviewed at least annually and filed with TRAI within seven working days of taking effect
AI Governance and Safety Committee led by a designated AI Governance and Safety Officer; pre-deployment approval by the officer
Three AI risk classes based on materiality (network/service significance, financial/operational effect, consumer consequences)
Inventory of all AI systems (active, inactive, decommissioned) with source, purpose and risk class; unlisted systems may not be deployed
Four incident severity levels (critical, high, moderate, low) using TEC standard 57090:2025 taxonomy; critical and high incidents reported to TRAI; central incident database
Supplier contracts must include regulatory compliance, audit rights, incident protocols and risk allocation; licensee remains accountable for third-party systems

Pre-deployment validation, conformity assessment (accuracy, robustness, explainability, fairness, drift, oversight) and impact assessment; grievance mechanism with central database of AI-related harms
confidence_note: Title, release date and open status confirmed on TRAI's consultation listing; provisions summarised from a law-firm note and press, not from the draft PDF. Deadline of 27 Nov 2026 from press. Counter-comment date not found.

title: DoT direction mandating pre-installation of the Sanchar Saathi application on mobile devices
issuing_body: Department of Telecommunications (DoT), AI & Digital Intelligence Unit

timeline.event: Telecom Cyber Security Rules 2024 amended (Rule 8 powers on IMEI/manufacturers)
Direction issued to manufacturers and importers
90-day deadline for pre-installation on new devices; compliance report due within 120 days

summary: Direction by DoT's AI & Digital Intelligence Unit under the Telecommunications Act 2023 and Telecom Cyber Security Rules 2024 requiring handset makers to pre-install the Sanchar Saathi fraud-reporting app, which feeds DoT's AI-based fraud and fake-document detection systems.
key_provisions: Issued under Rules 8(3), 8(4) and 8(8) of the Telecom Cyber Security Rules 2024 (as amended 22 Oct 2025) and the Telecommunications Act 2023
Pre-install Sanchar Saathi on all devices manufactured or imported within 90 days; app must be visible and not disabled; push to existing devices via software update
Compliance report to DoT within 120 days; non-compliance attracts action under the Act and Rules
DoT's AI & Digital Intelligence Unit uses AI/big data on Chakshu reports and subscriber data; DoT reported in July 2026 that its Fraud Risk Indicator prevented about ₹1,800 crore of cyber fraud
Press reports of a partial walk-back on the 'cannot be disabled' requirement (Dec 2025) were not verified against an amended order
confidence_note: Order date, issuing unit, legal basis and deadlines from MediaNama's reading of the signed order; DoT order PDF not retrieved. Reported partial rollback unverified.

title: TEC Standard 57050:2023 – Fairness Assessment and Rating of Artificial Intelligence Systems
issuing_body: Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC), Department of Telecommunications

timeline.event: TEC fairness assessment and rating standard published (2023)
TEC 57090:2025 (AI incident/robustness taxonomy) referenced by TRAI's October 2026 draft AI guidelines (reported)

summary: Voluntary TEC standard providing a procedure to assess and rate fairness of AI systems (bias risk assessment, metric thresholds, bias testing), used as a reference in telecom AI governance texts.
key_provisions: Three-step process: bias risk assessment, selection of fairness metrics and thresholds, and bias testing including scenario-based evaluation
Produces a fairness rating for AI systems; voluntary and applicable beyond telecom
TEC also publishes work on AI robustness; TEC 57090:2025 is cited by TRAI's 2026 draft for incident taxonomy (number per secondary source)
confidence_note: tec.gov.in could not be fetched (TLS error). Standard number and 2023 date rest on secondary and academic sources; the TEC 57090:2025 reference comes from one law-firm summary of the TRAI draft. Brief cross-reference only; BIS/TEC standards are covered by another researcher.

title: Computational Thinking and Artificial Intelligence Curriculum, Classes 3-8 (CBSE, under Ministry of Education direction)
issuing_body: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) / Ministry of Education, Department of School Education and Literacy

key_provisions: Classes 3-5: 50 hours per year of CT integrated with Mathematics and 'The World Around Us'; Classes 6-8: 100 hours per year covering advanced CT, data handling and early AI
AI concepts begin in Class 6; Classes 3-5 assessment linked to core subjects, Classes 6-8 assessed through projects and competency-based methods
Framework is platform-neutral and grounded in NEP 2020 and NCF-SE 2023
Expert committee chaired by Dr Karthik Raman (IIT Madras); implementation with KVS and NVS
Applies to CBSE-affiliated schools; state boards are not bound (state mandates covered by other researchers)
confidence_note: Official CBSE curriculum PDF read (hours, stages, committee). Circular number Acad-15/2026 and 1 April 2026 date come from secondary sources, not from the circular itself.

key_provisions: Four risk tiers (Low, Moderate, High, Critical) scored on eight inherent-risk factors; tier determines audit depth, frequency, independence and documentation

Names CERT-In, MeitY, RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and TRAI as regulators whose requirements are to be incorporated in audit criteria; a 'mandatory compliance scope' applies to in-scope organisations (government, PSUs, critical sectors) while others are encouraged to adopt
